page: The Microsoft Azure FX24-6mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 6 dedicated vCPUs across 3 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an expansive 260 MB L3 cache, complemented by Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector acceleration instruction sets. The machine features an extraordinary memory footprint of 504 GB of RAM, offering 84 GB per vCPU, alongside a bundled 1417 GB NVMe SSD local drive for low-latency scratch storage. No dedicated graphics processing units are included.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-threaded performance driven by the high 4.2 GHz clock rate. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2362.0 and text processing at 2948.0, reinforced by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 34.83 GB/sec. Due to the limited count of 6 vCPUs, multi-core throughput sits in the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7259.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12058.01. Memory read bandwidth reaches 518.54 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 51.2 GB/sec for large blocks. In-memory datastore evaluations demonstrate 9.51 million Redis SET operations per second, while LLM execution without hardware accelerators drops to 4.59 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX24-6mds_v2 presents an asymmetric profile characterized by exceptionally high memory and cache density per core. Because core counts are restrained, organizations running per-core software licenses can reduce licensing overhead while accessing extensive system memory and fast single-thread execution. This architecture fits large in-memory databases, memory-constrained electronic design automation (EDA) tooling, batch data transforms, and relational databases demanding high per-thread compute alongside rapid local NVMe temporary storage.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24-6mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 6 dedicated vCPUs (3 physical cores) operating at 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 504 GB of system RAM, yielding an exceptional 84 GB per core, and includes 1417 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without hardware GPU accelerators. Architectural highlights include a 260 MB L3 cache, AMX, and AVX-512 extensions. Benchmarks emphasize top-tier single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2362.0, along with sustained single-threaded compression throughput. With multi-threaded compute bounded by its 6-vCPU allocation, the instance provides high qualitative licensing efficiency for workloads sensitive to per-core costs. The FX24-6mds_v2 is suited for large-footprint in-memory databases, electronic design automation, financial simulation modeling, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines needing swift local ephemeral disk space.
